saints.name: Elizabeth the New Martyr
saints.dates: Modern period; exact chronology not established here

summary.text: Elizabeth is remembered as a grand duchess who entered Orthodoxy from a Protestant background and later founded a community devoted to service. The life describes her response to her husband's assassination and her death with companions during revolutionary persecution. It also notes the transfer of her and Barbara's bodies to Jerusalem. Her biography belongs to the history of Russia's new martyrs.

blocks.text: After her husband’s assassination, she visited his imprisoned killer and urged repentance. She devoted herself to the Martha and Mary community in Moscow, which combined a religious common life with nursing and care for poor people. Arrest in 1918 brought exile together with Sister Barbara.

blocks.text: At Alapaevsk in July 1918, Elizabeth, Barbara, and other members of the imperial family were thrown alive into a deep mine shaft. The diocesan account transmits reports from local people who heard singing below; it says the fall did not immediately kill the victims.

blocks.text: The diocesan account dates the killing to the night of July 17–18,1918 in civil reckoning. The older date July 5 in another church life reflects the Old Style calendar. The dates express different calendar conventions. It places the grand duchess and Sister Barbara among victims thrown alive into a deep mine shaft at Alapaevsk.

blocks.text: The bodies of Elizabeth and Barbara were eventually taken to Jerusalem and buried at the church of Mary Magdalene. She is remembered as a new martyr whose works of mercy preceded her imprisonment and violent death.
